{{DISPLAYTITLE:Esports World Cup 2024}} {{Tabs static |name1=Overview|link1=Esports World Cup/2024 |name2=Club Championship Standings|link2=Esports World Cup/2024/Club Championship Standings |name3=Player List|link3=Esports World Cup/2024/Player List }} {{Infobox league |name=Esports World Cup 2024 |shortname=EWC 2024 |series=Esports World Cup |liquipediatier=1 |image=Esports World Cup 2024 lightmode.png |imagedark=Esports World Cup 2024 darkmode.png |icon=Esports World Cup icon lightmode.png |icondarkmode=Esports World Cup icon darkmode.png |organizer1=EWC Foundation |organizer1-link=https://esportsworldcup.com/ |organizer2=ESL FACEIT Group |organizer2-link=https://eslfaceitgroup.com/ |organizer3=VSPO |organizer3-link=https://www.vsgo.com/ |type=Offline |country=Saudi Arabia |city=Riyadh |venue= |prizepoolusd=62,500,000 |website=https://esportsworldcup.com/ |rulebook=https://drive.google.com/file/d/1ew1qBq6k-5g-m8Olk_6LmJAY6grhTXgE/view |instagram=ewc_en |twitch=ewc |twitter=EWC_EN |youtube=@EWC |tiktok=eswcgg |facebook=EsportsWorldCup |kuaishou=3xkdx8xa7u5ymts |team_number=115 |sdate=2024-06-28 |edate=2024-08-25 |previous=Gamers8/2023{{!}}Gamers8 2023 |next=Esports_World_Cup/2025{{!}}EWC 2025 }} The '''2024 Esports World Cup''' is an ongoing multi-game tournament held in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, hosted by the Esports World Cup Foundation (EWCF) and ESL FACEIT Group. It is the first edition of the [[Esports World Cup]], a tournament series announced in late 2023 as a rebranding and expansion of [[Gamers8]]. The tournament features competitions in 22 different games, including ''[[dota2:Main Page|Dota 2]]'', ''[[mobilelegends:Main Page|Mobile Legends: Bang Bang]]'', ''[[pubg:Main Page|PUBG Mobile]]'', ''[[arenaofvalor:Main Page|Honor of Kings]]'', ''[[apexlegends:Main Page|Apex Legends]]'', ''[[rainbowsix:Main Page|Rainbow Six Siege]]'', and more. Each game has its own independent structure for qualifying, but the championship series for each title forms part of the Esports World Cup. Alongside the competitions in the games, there is a Club Competition across all games for participating organizations. ==Events== {{Liquipedia_links/Esports_World_Cup_2024}} ==Club Program== On February 1st, 2024, the EWCF announced the Esports World Cup Club Program "designed to promote sustainable planning" for organizations. The EWCF initially announced that 28 organizations would participate; 22 via direct invitation and 6 via an open application process.{{cite web|url=https://twitter.com/ESWCgg/status/1753055666279735739|title=It’s time to unveil the #EWC Club Program, a first-of-its-kind initiative designed to promote sustainable planning for all participating esports clubs|date=2024-02-01|author=Esports World Cup|language={{FlagNoLink|usuk}} English}} This was later expanded to 8 open applicant teams as the teams were announced on May 5th, 2024, totaling 30 partnered teams.{{cite web|url=https://twitter.com/ESWCgg/status/1787467602232508731|title=30 esports Clubs join Esports World Cup Foundation Club Support Program|date=2024-05-06|author=Esports World Cup|language={{FlagNoLink|usuk}} English}} Selected organizations are eligible for an annual six-figure payout to support their operations, as well as funding teams' entrances into featured titles at the Esports World Cup. These organizations are also able to gain financial rewards based on their performance in driving viewership and fan engagement to the event. Esports organizations applying through the open application first had to submit an application between February 1st and February 15th. Successful applications then had to pitch their submission to the Esports World Club committee.{{cite web|url=https://ewcclubprogram.com/|title=EWC CLUB PROGRAM|date=2024-02-01|author=Esports World Cup|language={{FlagNoLink|usuk}} English}} Being a part of the Club Support program does not guarantee participation in the EWC tournaments; teams still need to qualify for the Esports World Cup on their own merit. ==Club Championship== A prizepool of $20,000,000 {{Abbr/USD}} is awarded to the top 16 organizations in the Club Championship. With the winning team gaining $7,000,000 {{Abbr/USD}}. Teams are awarded points in the overall ranking by finishing in the top 8 of a tournament, with a first place giving a 1000 points total. To win the Championship however, a team needs to also win at least 1 of the 23 tournaments. {{cite web|url=https://twitter.com/ESWCgg/status/1790405780635537870|title=What is this #EsportsWorldCup Club Championship all about?!|date=2024-05-14|author=Esports World Cup|language={{FlagNoLink|usuk}} English}} This Championship is open to '''all organizations''' competing in the EWC, regardless of if they are a part of the Club Program or not. However, organizations had to declare a public '''roster entry''' prior to {{countdown|date=June 13, 2024 - 23:59 {{Abbr/AST}}|rawdatetime=true}} to be eligible for points in that respective game. The deadline was extended to {{countdown|date=June 27, 2024 - 23:59 {{Abbr/AST}}|rawdatetime=true}} specifically for Call of Duty events. ===Prize Pool=== The total prize pool of the tournament, including the EWC Club Championship, the Game Championships, the MVP Awards and the EWC Qualifiers is $62,500,000 {{Abbr/USD}}. $20,000,000 {{Abbr/USD}} are spread among the organizations in the Club Championship as seen below: {{box|start|padding=2em}}

==Controversy== The Esports World Cup has been accused of [[wikipedia:sportswashing|sportswashing]] — using high-profile events to project a positive image around the world, to distract others from controversies such as human rights records. The Gamers8 event of 2023 drew sportwashing concerns over Saudi Arabia's human rights record,{{cite web|url=https://www.dexerto.com/esports/gamers8-2023-schedule-esports-tournaments-prize-and-controversy-explained-2101989/|title=Gamers8 2023: Schedule, esports tournaments, prize and controversy explained|publisher=Dexerto|author=Luís Mira|date=2023-06-07|language={{FlagNoLink|usuk}} English}}{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4EcwvndASNw|title=Esportswashing WORKS - Gamers8 And The Saudi Sellouts|author=Richard Lewis|date=2023-09-15|language={{FlagNoLink|usuk}} English}} and the 2024 event saw the controversy return,{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cq5x85zd71eo|title=Esports World Cup boss defends holding event in Saudi Arabia|publisher=BBC|author=Andrew Rogers|date=2024-07-04|language={{FlagNoLink|usuk}} English}}{{cite web|url=https://edition.cnn.com/2024/07/06/sport/esports-world-cup-saudi-arabia-spt-intl/index.html|title=A new esports tournament in Saudi Arabia promises to be a game-changer – but it’s also caused division in the industry|publisher=CNN|author=Ben Church|date=2024-07-06|language={{FlagNoLink|usuk}} English}} with the New York Times noting parallels to Saudi Arabia's actions in other sports such as football and golf, with the Esports World Cup seen as the esports arm.{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5237849/2024/02/02/saudi-arabia-sport-investments/|title=Saudi Arabia’s takeover of world sport: Football, golf, boxing and now tennis?|publisher=New York Times|author=Joey D'Urso|date=2024-02-02|language={{FlagNoLink|usuk}} English}} In 2023, in an interview with Fox News, [[wikipedia:Mohammed bin Salman|Mohammed bin Salman]], Crown Prince and Prime Minister of Saudi Arabia, stated he "doesn't care" about accusations of sportswashing, as it was beneficial for Saudi Arabia's economy.{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2023/sep/21/mohammed-bin-salman-says-he-will-continue-doing-sport-washing-for-saudi-arabia|title=Mohammed bin Salman says he will ‘continue doing sport washing’ for Saudi Arabia|publisher=The Guardian|author=Paul MacInnes|date=2023-09-21|language={{FlagNoLink|usuk}} English}} In response to the concerns, Esports World Cup Foundation CEO Ralf Reichert, in an interview with the BBC, reassured LGBT fans and players over their safety, and promised no discrimination, although local norms and cultures had to be respected. [[Team Liquid]], one of the largest esports organizations, chose to take part in the tournament, to use the event as a platform to show their support for LGBT people. The previous year, Team Liquid had pledged $50,000 in donations to LGBTQ+ charity Rainbow Railroad in response to their team's participation in [[dota2:Riyadh Masters/2023|Riyadh Masters 2023]], with CEO Victor Goossens stating that it would be difficult for the organization to attract and retain top talent if they refused to play in these events, but that they would stand by its values of diversity and inclusion, even during these events, and he personally had no issue calling out Saudi Arabia's human rights record.{{cite web|url=https://www.dexerto.com/dota2/team-liquid-donates-50000-to-lgbtq-charity-in-response-to-riyadh-masters-participation-2212570/|title=Team Liquid donates $50,000 to LGBTQ+ charity in response to Riyadh Masters participation|publisher=Dexerto|author=Declan Mclaughlin|date=2023-07-14|language={{FlagNoLink|usuk}} English}} For the 2024 event, Team Liquid announced that they would be wearing the Pride flag on their jerseys at events throughout the summer — including the Esports World Cup.{{cite web|url=https://dotesports.com/general/news/team-liquid-teams-get-ok-to-wear-pride-jerseys-at-saudi-arabias-esports-world-cup|title=Team Liquid teams get OK to wear Pride jerseys at Saudi Arabia’s Esports World Cup |publisher=Dot Esports|author=Issac McIntyre and Mika Permana Wahjudi|date=2024-07-03|language={{FlagNoLink|usuk}} English}}{{cite web|url=https://x.com/TeamLiquid/status/1802053754092445702|title=We’re starting the LCS Summer Split in style competing in our 2024 Pride Jersey. We’ll be wearing this around the world throughout the summer.|author=Team Liquid|date=2024-06-15|language={{FlagNoLink|usuk}} English}} Goossens and fellow Team Liquid CEO Steve Arhancet also released lengthy statements discussing their decision to participate in the Esports World Cup.{{cite web|url=https://www.outsports.com/2024/7/8/24097274/steve-arhancet-team-liquid-pride-jersey-esports-world-cup-gay-lgbtq-saudi-arabia/|title=Gay owner of pro team speaks out on Saudi Arabia’s abuses, wears Pride jersey in Riyadh|publisher=Outsports|author=Jon Holmes|date=2024-07-08|language={{FlagNoLink|usuk}} English}}{{cite web|url=https://x.com/LiquidNazgul/status/1800216288062763071|title=On our participation in the Esports World Cup:|author=Victor Goossens|date=2024-06-10|language={{FlagNoLink|usuk}} English}}{{cite web|url=https://x.com/LiQuiD112/status/1800260015359447256|title=In my last retweet, Victor explains the competitive and commercial considerations that influenced our choice to participate in this year’s inaugural EWC. We have not come to this decision lightly, and the video details our concerns about human rights in Saudi Arabia, the|author=Steve Arhancet|date=2024-06-10|language={{FlagNoLink|usuk}} English}} Team Liquid's stance received both positive and negative reactions, including those from trans people in esports. [[Riot Games]] granted a license to host a ''League of Legends'' tournament at the Esports World Cup, despite having previously withdrawn their support for the Saudi [[wikipedia:Neom|NEOM]] project after criticism. Journalist Jacob Wolf reported that internal Riot Games feedback towards a hypothetical ''League of Legends'' event at the Esports World Cup was negative.{{cite web|url=https://x.com/JacobWolf/status/1743358397464883396|title=Been told internal discourse among employees at Riot, since I reported earlier this week that League will be at the Esports World Cup in Saudi, has been not great. An internal leader for the EMEA LGBTQ+ ERG even defended the decision, too.|author=Jacob Wolf|date=2024-01-05|language={{FlagNoLink|usuk}} English}} In response, interviewer Travis Gafford stated he would not cover nor watch the Esports World Cup, releasing a video to raise funds for Amnesty International in return.{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TSwqlRHQObA|title=Why I will not Cover or Watch the Esports World Cup|author=Travis Gafford|date=2024-04-24|language={{FlagNoLink|usuk}} English}} [[leagueoflegends:FlyQuest|FlyQuest]], who qualified for the Esports World Cup, chose to let their players, coaches and staff members decide whether they would participate or not, and that they would support their decisions.{{cite web|url=https://x.com/FlyQuest/status/1794065943641092142|title=FlyQuest strives for competitive excellence in every esports title we participate in — and through hard work and dedication, FlyQuest players and teams across multiple titles have earned the right to compete at the 2024 Esports World Cup.|author=FlyQuest|date=2024-05-24|language={{FlagNoLink|usuk}} English}} FlyQuest took part in the [[leagueoflegends:Esports_World_Cup/2024|event]] in the end, finishing joint-last. Wolf estimated that $100m was spent on the ''League of Legends'' event alone.{{cite web|url=https://x.com/JacobWolf/status/1808913349779820952|title=@amaxlegit The LCS & LEC are scaling down. The Saudis invested likely more than $100M in this one event. That’s why.|author=Jacob Wolf|date=2024-07-04|language={{FlagNoLink|usuk}} English}} Within ''Overwatch'', team [[overwatch:Ex Oblivione|Ex Oblivione]] announced they would take part in the qualifiers for the Esports World Cup, but would decline to play in Riyadh if they qualified.{{cite web|url=https://esports-news.co.uk/2024/03/29/ex-oblivione-overwatch-2-esports-world-cup/|title=Ex Oblivione refuse to compete in Overwatch 2 Esports World Cup: ‘We value inclusivity and equality’|publisher=Esports News UK|author=Dom Sacco|date=2024-03-29|language={{FlagNoLink|usuk}} English}} Ex Oblivione did not qualify for the event. [[overwatch:ENCE|ENCE]]'s [[overwatch:Masaa|Masaa]], who did qualify, chose to drop out of the event, citing disagreements with Saudi Arabia's stance on LGBT rights and other moral issues.{{cite web|url=https://www.esports.net/news/overwatch/masaa-esports-world-cup-overwatch/|title=Masaa Drops out of Esports World Cup Overwatch Event|publisher=Esports.net|author=Jordan Ashley|date=2024-07-05|language={{FlagNoLink|usuk}} English}} ''Rainbow Six'' shoutcaster [[rainbowsix:Dezachu|Dezachu]] claimed that participating organizations at the Esports World Cup signed a legally-binding contract not to criticize the Esports World Cup, Saudi Arabia or its government, and were also contractually-obligated to tweet positive things about the event and produce promotional content.{{cite web|url=https://x.com/Dezachu/status/1799127365391421733|title=Any org attending the EWC is signing a legally binding contract stating they (their players, their staff, creators, you name it) cannot say a bad word about the EWC, Saudi Arabia, or its government.|author=Dezachu|date=2024-06-07|language={{FlagNoLink|usuk}} English}} Separately, the Esports World Cup Foundation announced a partnership with the Esports Awards, where the awards ceremonies would be held in Riyadh. In light of this announcement, several people announced they would not be involved going forwards,{{cite web|url=https://esports.gg/news/streamers/esports-awards-esports-world-cup-backlash/|title=Esports Awards faces major backlash for Esports World Cup partnership|publisher=Esports.gg|author=Tom Bull|date=2024-06-09|language={{FlagNoLink|usuk}} English}} including [[valorant:Goldenboy|Goldenboy]],{{cite web|url=https://x.com/GoldenboyFTW/status/1799423927069856003|title=Hey everyone, I'm going to get straight to the point: I won't be hosting the Esports Awards moving forward, and I will be resigning from the panel effective immediately. I'm extremely disappointed in the higher-ups at ESA for the direction they're taking their business, but it's|author=Goldenboy|date=2024-06-08|language={{FlagNoLink|usuk}} English}} a host for the Esports Awards and in multiple esports, and committee members Parker Mackay{{cite web|url=https://x.com/INTERRO/status/1799136678461972892|title=I spent ~4 years on the Esports Awards committee. I resigned this morning. I am extremely proud that the Siege scene pushes for a welcoming, tolerant, and inclusive place for all. These are our values and I'll always fight for them|author=Parker Mackay|date=2024-06-07|language={{FlagNoLink|usuk}} English}} and PGL CEO Silviu Stroie.{{cite web|url=https://x.com/ssilviu/status/1799174932980764843|title=I've been a panelist for this event since last year. After today's announcement I've mailed them to get removed from anything related to it. Panels, mailing lists, anything. I cannot be associated with such a mockery|author=Silviu Stroie|date=2024-06-07|language={{FlagNoLink|usuk}} English}} ==References== {{Reflist}}

It is the second edition of the [[Esports World Cup]], a tournament series announced in late 2023 as a rebranding and expansion of [[Gamers8]]. Each game has its own independent structure for qualifying, but the championship series for each title forms part of the Esports World Cup. Alongside the competitions in the games, there is a Club Competition across all games for participating organizations. ==Events== {{Liquipedia links/Esports World Cup 2025}} ==Club Program== On February 1st, 2024, the EWCF announced the Esports World Cup Club Program "designed to promote sustainable planning" for organizations.{{cite web|url=https://twitter.com/ESWCgg/status/1753055666279735739|title=It’s time to unveil the #EWC Club Program, a first-of-its-kind initiative designed to promote sustainable planning for all participating esports clubs|date=2024-02-01|author=Esports World Cup|language={{FlagNoLink|usuk}} English}} Selected organizations are eligible for an annual six-figure payout to support their operations, as well as funding teams' entrances into featured titles at the Esports World Cup. These organizations are also able to gain financial rewards based on their performance in driving viewership and fan engagement to the event. Being a part of the Club Support program does not guarantee participation in the EWC tournaments; teams still need to qualify for the Esports World Cup on their own merit. ===Changes to 2025 Club Program=== * Application phase from December 10th, 2024 - January 10th, 2025.{{cite web|url=https://esportsworldcup.com/en/clubprogram|title=EWC CLUB PROGRAM|date=2024-12-10|author=Esports World Cup|language={{FlagNoLink|usuk}} English}} * Final selection will be done no later than February 28th, 2025 * '''Total number of teams increased from 30 to 40 teams ** 32 spots will be reserved for ''Open Signups'' ** Up to 8 ''Direct Invite'' spots reserved for the Top 8 Teams from the [[Esports_World_Cup/2024/Club_Championship_Standings|2024 Club Championship]] ==Club Championship== A prizepool of $27,000,000 {{Abbr/USD}} is awarded to the top 24 organizations in the Club Championship, with the winning team gaining $7,000,000 {{Abbr/USD}}. Each event awarded points to teams within the top 8. To win the Championship however, a team needs to also win at least 1 tournament. {{cite web|url=https://twitter.com/ESWCgg/status/1790405780635537870|title=What is this #EsportsWorldCup Club Championship all about?!|date=2024-05-14|author=Esports World Cup|language={{FlagNoLink|usuk}} English}} This Championship is open to '''all organizations''' competing in the EWC, regardless of if they are a part of the Club Program or not. However, each Club has to settle on their competing titles and the respective rosters for EWC '''''publicly''''' '''by {{countdown|date=May 15th, 2025 - 23:59 {{Abbr/AST}}|rawdatetime=true}}''' prior to a set date to be eligible for points in that respective game. This affects signings and acquisitions of new squads or 1on1 players, not minor roster changes in team games, which are regulated separately in each tournament's rulebook. '''''For {{leagueIconSmall/fc25}} EA SPORTS FC 25 and {{leagueIconSmall/apex}} Apex Legends, deadline was extended to the different date of {{countdown|date=May 31st, 2025 - 23:59 {{Abbr/AST}}|rawdatetime=true}}.'''''{{cite web|url=https://x.com/EWC_EN/status/1924859688769720604|title=An Update On The EWC25 Club Championship|date=2025-05-20|author=Esports World Cup|language={{FlagNoLink|usuk}} English}} ===Changes to 2025 Club Championship=== * '''Joint Ventures''' (a collaboration between two distinct organization on a specific roster) are ineligible for Points scoring ** ''For example: [[mobilelegends:Falcons AP.Bren|Falcons AP.Bren]], [[mobilelegends:Fnatic ONIC|Fnatic ONIC]], [[mobilelegends:NIP Flash|NiP x Flash]] are Joint Ventures ** Joint Ventures that are not intended for Points are only allowed if the rulebook permits * For a roster to be eligible for Points, Clubs required to have '''One aligned name''' throughout the EWC * Exemptions may be handed, i.e. publisher requirements * Prize Pool increased by $7,000,000 compared to 2024 ===Prize Pool=== The total prize pool of the tournament, including the EWC Club Championship, the Game Championships, the MVP Awards and the EWC Qualifiers is over $70,450,000 {{Abbr/USD}}. * '''If clubs tied with same points but not involved 1st place ** Related clubs then split the prize pool equally by combining prize from all tied placements, then divded by number of tied teams *** (Example: a tie between 4th & 5th will result in $2,500,000 and $2,000,000 from both 4th/5th individually combined together into 1 pool, then split equally to two teams) * '''If clubs tied with same points but involves 1st place ** Tiebreakers are in the following order: *** Number of tournament wins *** More points from direct matches

{{DISPLAYTITLE:Esports World Cup 2026}} {{EWC26 Tabs}} {{Infobox league |liquipediatier=1 |name=Esports World Cup 2026 |shortname=EWC 2026 |series=Esports World Cup |image=Esports World Cup 2026 lightmode.png |imagedark=Esports World Cup 2026 darkmode.png |icon=Esports World Cup icon lightmode.png |icondarkmode=Esports World Cup icon darkmode.png |organizer1=Esports Foundation |organizer1-link=https://esportsworldcup.com/ |organizer2=ESL FACEIT Group |organizer2-link=https://eslfaceitgroup.com/ |type=Offline |country=fr |city=Paris |venue1link=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris_Expo_Porte_de_Versailles|venue=Paris Expo Porte de Versailles |prizepoolusd=75,000,000 |website=https://esportsworldcup.com/ |rulebook= |instagram=ewc_en |twitch=ewc |twitter=EWC_EN |youtube=@EWC |tiktok=ewc_en |facebook=EsportsWorldCup |kuaishou=3xkdx8xa7u5ymts |rulebook=https://d3h9qea4qy4169.cloudfront.net/EWC_2026_Global_Rulebook_1_1_55b3cc60e1.pdf |rulebook2={{fullurl:File:EWC_2026_Global_Rulebook.pdf}} |sdate=2026-07-02 |edate=2026-08-23 |previous=Esports_World_Cup/2025{{!}}2025 |next=Esports_World_Cup/2027{{!}}2027 }} The '''2026 Esports World Cup''' is an upcoming multi-game esports tournament held in Paris, France, hosted by the Esports Foundation (EF) and ESL FACEIT Group. It is the third edition of the [[Esports World Cup]], a tournament series announced in late 2023 as a rebranding and expansion of [[Gamers8]]. In 2027, the EWC will also be joined by their Nation-based equivalent, the [[Esports Nations Cup/2026|Esports Nations Cup]]. Each game has its own independent structure for qualifying, but the championship series for each title forms part of the Esports World Cup. Alongside the competitions in the games, there is a Club Competition across all games for participating organizations. The tournament will mark the first EWC edition to be hosted outside of Saudi Arabia. Due to the ongoing [[:wikipedia:2026_Iran_war|2026 Iran war]], a relocation announcement was made on May 20th.{{Cite web|url=https://esportsworldcup.com/en/news/ewc26-to-be-hosted-in-paris-france |title=Esports World Cup 2026 to be hosted in Paris, France |author=Esports World Cup |date=2026-05-20}} ==Events== {{Liquipedia links/Esports World Cup 2026}} ==Club Program== On February 1st, 2024, the EWCF announced the Esports World Cup Club Program "designed to promote sustainable planning" for organizations.{{cite web|url=https://twitter.com/ESWCgg/status/1753055666279735739|title=It’s time to unveil the #EWC Club Program, a first-of-its-kind initiative designed to promote sustainable planning for all participating esports clubs|date=2024-02-01|author=Esports World Cup|language={{FlagNoLink|usuk}} English}} Selected organizations are eligible for an annual six-figure payout to support their operations, as well as funding teams' entrances into featured titles at the Esports World Cup. These organizations are also able to gain financial rewards based on their performance in driving viewership and fan engagement to the event. Being a part of the Club Support program does not guarantee participation in the EWC tournaments; teams still need to qualify for the Esports World Cup on their own merit. ===Changes to 2025 Club Program=== * Application phase from November 18th - December 19th, 2025. * Final selection will be done no later than March 31st, 2026 ** 32 spots will be reserved for ''Open Signups'' ** Up to 8 ''Direct Invite'' spots reserved for the Top 8 Teams from the [[Esports_World_Cup/2025/Club_Championship_Standings|2025 Club Championship]] ==Club Championship== A prizepool of $30,000,000 {{Abbr/USD}} is awarded to the top 24 organizations in the Club Championship. With the winning team gaining $7,000,000 {{Abbr/USD}}. Each event awarded points to teams within the top 8. To win the Championship however, a team needs to also win at least 1 tournament. {{cite web|url=https://twitter.com/ESWCgg/status/1790405780635537870|title=What is this #EsportsWorldCup Club Championship all about?!|date=2024-05-14|author=Esports World Cup|language={{FlagNoLink|usuk}} English}} This Championship is open to '''all organizations''' competing in the EWC, regardless of if they are a part of the Club Program or not. Each Club must finalize their players contract and rosters announcement '''''publicly''''' '''by {{countdown|date=April 30th, 2026 - 23:59 {{Abbr/AST}}|rawdatetime=true}}''' in order to be eligible for points in that respective game. This affects signings and acquisitions of new squads or 1on1 players, not minor roster changes in team games, which are regulated separately in each tournament's rulebook. As such the tournament name may be rebranded to be part of the game's roadmap instead of the standard EWC naming.
